en: A bill becomes a law when both the Senate and House of Representatives approve it and the President signs it.
The bayanihan tradition works when neighbors physically carry a nipa hut to help a family relocate to a new community site.
Aguinaldo unfurled the Philippine flag and played the national anthem to officially signal the end of Spanish colonial rule in Kawit.
Ifugao farmers carve mountain slopes into stepped terraces, which slows water runoff and prevents soil erosion during heavy tropical rains.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator that uses local materials to keep premature babies warm in rural areas lacking electricity.
Sinulog dancers step forward and backward to mimic the river current, which creates a rhythmic prayer dance honoring the Santo Niño.
Ancient Filipinos carved Baybayin characters on bamboo stems, which allowed them to record messages before the Spanish introduced the Latin alphabet.
Younger Filipinos perform pagmamano by pressing an elder's hand to their forehead, which shows deep respect and requests a blessing.
Registered citizens cast their secret ballots during elections, which directly determines the officials who will lead the government branches.
Jose Rizal wrote Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish abuses, which awakened Filipino nationalism and inspired the revolution.
Farmers use the carabao to plow muddy rice paddies, which efficiently breaks up the hard soil to prepare it for planting.
Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument with multiple figures holding bolos, which visually represents the united masses fighting for Philippine independence.
